standard_prerequisites.name: Transcendence degree as the dimension of the closure of a point in the fibre, and the dimension formula for fibres after base change

standard_prerequisites.use: The first converts between the dimension of a closed subset of the fibre and the transcendence degree at its points, giving the equivalence even fibre by fibre, and the second two give the base change statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: Openness of the flat locus inside a fibre
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter flat.tex, label lemma-open-in-fibre-where-flat, invoked in the statement at proof line 6278
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the set of points of a fibre where the module is not flat a closed subset, so that its dimension is defined.

core_obligations: Translate the conditions pointwise: for a point of the source over a point of the base, the dimension of the closure of that point in the fibre equals the transcendence degree of its residue field over that of the base, so the two conditions are equivalent fibre by fibre (proof lines 6286-6294).
Conversely, if a closed subset of a fibre has dimension d then it contains a point whose transcendence degree is d, which completes the equivalence (proof lines 6291-6294).
Record invariance under base change from the corresponding statements for the flat locus and the fibre dimension (proof lines 6295-6297).
proof_roadmap: Pointwise translation of the two conditions (proof lines 6286-6290).
Converse direction via a point of maximal transcendence degree (proof lines 6291-6294).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows the equivalence of two formulations of the statement that the non flat locus of a finite type module has fibre dimension below n, and that the property is stable under base change (statement lines 6270-6284, tag 05ME-adjacent). The proof translates between the dimension of a closed subset of a fibre and the transcendence degree of the residue field at its points, obtaining the equivalence fibre by fibre, and then quotes the base change statements. The translation is the substance, so the claim is H2.
